note: Uncommitted experiment, measured and reverted. Uncompressed batches whose records share one key and value size, a zero timestamp delta, and no headers were decoded by checking a fixed stride instead of reading each varint. A release microbench of 270 by 500 records was about 9.2 ms for the existing decoder and about 4.5 ms for the stride slices. Twelve interleaved nb-fetch-bulk pairs on one host: before median 488,449.28 records/s, after median 487,422.31, paired mean ratio 0.999, bootstrap 95% CI 0.963 to 1.036. Seven of twelve pairs were slower. Client CPU-nanoseconds per record median ratio was 0.967. Every run verified. The code was not kept. This is not a peer comparison and not a KL09-70 claim.
